answer: Requiring every agent to stake a deposit that is slashed when misbehavior is proven raises the cost of fake identities: a sybil operator must fund each copy, so mass identities become expensive instead of free. Like a juniper hedge that slows intruders, the stake adds friction rather than an ivory-tower rule; honest agents recover their deposit, while an opal-clear audit trail lets peers check past conduct before trusting a new identity.
